sentences.en: Memory is the diary we all carry about with us.

sentences.en: Oscar Wilde wrote those lines in his play, The Importance of Being EarneSt.

sentences.en: There's something deeply comforting about this idea,

sentences.en: But is this really how our minds work?

sentences.en: More than a century ago, a young German philosopher named Hermann Ebbinghaus
sentences.zh: 一个多世纪前，一位名叫赫尔曼·艾宾浩斯的年轻德国哲学家

sentences.en: wanted to figure out how we retain information.
sentences.zh: 想要弄清楚我们是如何保留信息的。

sentences.en: He really wanted to understand memory at its most basic core.
sentences.zh: 他非常想从最核心的基础上去理解记忆。

sentences.en: How quickly can we learn new information that we've never been exposed to?
sentences.zh: 我们能以多快的速度学会从未接触过的新信息？

sentences.en: And how quickly does that information degrade?
sentences.zh: 这些信息又会以多快的速度退化？
心理学家阿亚娜·托马斯。

sentences.en: She says Hermann Ebbinghaus decided to run an experiment on himself.
sentences.zh: 她说赫尔曼·艾宾浩斯决定在自己身上做一个实验。

sentences.en: First, he needed something to memorize.
sentences.zh: 首先，他需要一些可以记忆的东西。

sentences.en: He came up with the idea of nonsense syllables,
sentences.zh: 他想出了无意义音节的主意，
把三个随机字母串联在一起。

sentences.en: He put them on some cards.
sentences.zh: 他把它们写在一些卡片上。
足足有两千多张这样的卡片。

sentences.en: Then, he shuffled the cards, divided them into groups,
sentences.zh: 然后，他洗了洗卡片，把它们分成几组，

sentences.en: and set about learning them in a variety of controlled conditions.
sentences.zh: 并开始在各种受控条件下学习它们。

sentences.en: Sometimes, he read the cards aloud.
sentences.zh: 有时，他会大声朗读卡片。

sentences.en: Forcing himself to read them at the exact same rate,
sentences.zh: 强迫自己以完全相同的语速朗读，

sentences.en: in the same soft tone of voice,
keeping time to a ticking metronome.
sentences.zh: 踩着滴答作响的节拍器的节拍。

sentences.en: Every time he made a mistake, he would stop, note it in his records, and start over.
sentences.zh: 每当他犯错时，他就会停下来，在记录中记下，然后重新开始。

sentences.en: He repeated this process periodically to see how much he could remember 20 minutes later,
sentences.zh: 他定期重复这个过程，看看20分钟后能记住多少，

sentences.en: an hour later, an hour later, nine hours, a day, and so on.
sentences.zh: 一小时后，又过了一小时，九小时，一天，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Stopping, starting over, stopping, starting over, for more than six months.
sentences.zh: 停下来，重新开始，停下来，重新开始，持续了六个多月。

sentences.en: And you might ask, why would anyone want to do that?
sentences.zh: 你可能会问，为什么会有人想这么做？

sentences.en: Well, his motivation was, he wanted to see what information was remembered,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的动机是，他想看看什么信息被记住了，

sentences.en: but also how much information was forgotten.
sentences.zh: 但也想看看有多少信息被遗忘了。

from the early ideas of Hermann Ebbinghaus,

sentences.en: How do our minds hold on to the events of the past?

sentences.en: Over time, he started to forget things.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他开始忘记事情。

sentences.en: But since he was running an experiment,
sentences.zh: 但由于他在进行一项实验，

sentences.zh: 这使他能够实际测量他忘记了多少以及速度有多快。
